correctness.rationale: For every n the Rudin–Shapiro parity-11 definition yields the exact recurrence r(2t)=r(t), r(2t+1)=r(t) XOR (t mod 2). A complete four-residue argument shows that (1,8m−1,8m,8m+1) matches the binary value at every n for every m≥1. The four-state substitution follows from the same recurrence, and the complete set of 65-factors is proved by 33792 certified substitution-closure memberships: 512 factors in sigma^10(A), closed under sigma. Since a length-65 window after substitution spans at most 33 source letters, the closure proves that no new 65-factor appears in any later iterate; the initial factors remain as prefixes. Coding gives the exact 512 binary factors. The executable then exhausts all C(64,4)=635376 shift tuples and retains the exact 24 list. Independent direct binary-digit and through-shift-32 enumerations corroborate the computations. No finite test is substituted for the symbolic infinite-family proof.

value.rationale: Four is the published minimum possible pseudoperiod cardinality for the classical Rudin–Shapiro automatic word. Giving an infinite progression of distinct optimal-cardinality tuples is a structural theorem, not a changed notation for a fixed witness. The complete exact shift-64 census is a motivated finite cutoff at a natural dyadic scale: it classifies 635376 candidates from the entire infinite word, not a sampled prefix, and supplies reproducible data for the unsolved general spectrum.
